threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You ask for directions to the nearest tube and everyone points you to a bus stop instead. Clearly, you haven't figured out 'it's quicker on the 30.'
Caught the N155 last night and some bloke was trying to sell a selfie stick. Said it was 'for capturing the night.' Just another typical journey.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I found a group of guys outside my window debating the pros and cons of falafel spots at 3am, I knew I was home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do you find graffiti-covered buses doubling as art spaces, a testament to the city's wild blend of chaos and creativity.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only a true local would know to avoid 16th and Mission during rush hour unless you want to witness a spontaneous street performance of chaos.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy at the Muni stop serenading pigeons with an old guitar. They seemed into it—one even fluffed its feathers like it was grooving.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think they can get an acai bowl anywhere, but locals know that the best smoothies are at the hidden fruit stall on Carrer de Fraternitat.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by their puzzled looks at the ticket machines. Locals zip through without a second glance, while newcomers are still deciphering the options.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think every café is overpriced until you find that tucked-away spot with the best flat white. Welcome to the hunt!
Last night on the 196, a bloke serenaded us with a ukulele while the driver pretended to be unimpressed. Classic Brixton vibes.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The way the old Turkish baker remembers everyone's name and asks about their kids. That's when it hit me; this place isn't just a stop, it's home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you hear a techno rave while waiting for a bus. It's like the city's heartbeat has its own soundtrack.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by their ability to seamlessly dodge the persistent BART delays while juggling burritos on their way to the park.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy on the 31 out-dancing everyone during a packed commute. Muni's the stage; you just never know who's dropping a performance!

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think every bar serves mojitos. In Gràcia, it’s definitely more about vermut and tapas—no fancy cocktails needed.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their struggle with the metro map—always staring at it like it’s a magic puzzle. Longtime locals know the shortcuts.
